headline: Chromatin contacts and methylation constrain gene regulation across tissues and disease
label: Chromatin Architecture And Gene Regulation
summary: Single-cell multiomics and foundation-model analyses now link 3D genome architecture to transcription in human tissues and Alzheimer's disease.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of chromatin architecture and epigenomic states as readouts of gene regulation. A foundation model trained on a 33-million-transcriptome collection shows that TADs are regions of elevated co-regulation, using consensus TAD maps for human and mouse. A framework integrating Hi-C, ChIA-PET and ENCODE cCREs classifies promoter-enhancer interactions and dual-state regulatory elements. Chromatin states are shown to drive cfDNA fragmentation, and single-cell multiomics in human retina and Alzheimer's brain jointly profile accessibility, methylation, 3D architecture and expression. Blood methylation predicts lineage gene expression but not stimulus-responsive checkpoint genes, marking limits of methylation as a proxy. DPCGS links GWAS associations to cell types through calibrated scRNA-seq gene-set scoring. What is new is joint measurement of the 3D genome and transcriptome within the same cells, paired with predictive models that test where regulatory information is and is not recoverable.
